audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 1 draft aligned to Hannah, Elkanah, Peninnah, Shiloh prayer, vow, Samuel's birth, weaning, and dedication narrative; later source/witness audit required.
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew-first naming, restored/mystical separation, narrative ambiguity, institutional power, vulnerable persons, violence, and misuse risks.

verses.restored: Now there was one man from Ramathaim-zophim, from hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.

familiar.text: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaimzophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite:

modern.text: Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֜ד מִן הָרָמָתַ֛יִם צוֹפִ֖ים מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמ֡וֹ אֶ֠לְקָנָה בֶּן יְרֹחָ֧ם בֶּן אֱלִיה֛וּא בֶּן תֹּ֥חוּ בֶן צ֖וּף אֶפְרָתִֽי

verses.restored: He had two wives. Name of one was Hannah, and name of second Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

familiar.text: And he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

modern.text: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

original.text: וְלוֹ֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֔ים שֵׁ֤ם אַחַת֙ חַנָּ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פְּנִנָּ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י לִפְנִנָּה֙ יְלָדִ֔ים וּלְחַנָּ֖ה אֵ֥ין יְלָדִֽים

verses.restored: That man went up from his city from days to days to bow down and sacrifice to YHWH of armies at Shiloh. There the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to YHWH.

familiar.text: And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were there.

modern.text: Year after year Elkanah would go up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.

original.text: וְעָלָה֩ הָאִ֨ישׁ הַה֤וּא מֵֽעִירוֹ֙ מִיָּמִ֣ים יָמִ֔ימָה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֧ת וְלִזְבֹּ֛חַ לַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּשִׁלֹ֑ה וְשָׁ֞ם שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי עֵלִ֗י חָפְנִי֙ וּפִ֣נְחָ֔ס כֹּהֲנִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: When day came and Elkanah sacrificed, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters.

familiar.text: And when the time was that Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions:

modern.text: And whenever the day came for Elkanah to present his sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיִּזְבַּ֖ח אֶלְקָנָ֑ה וְנָתַ֞ן לִפְנִנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּֽלְכָל בָּנֶ֛יהָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ מָנֽוֹת

verses.restored: But to Hannah he gave one double/choice portion, because he loved Hannah, though YHWH had closed her womb.

familiar.text: But unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion; for he loved Hannah: but the LORD had shut up her womb.

modern.text: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved her even though the LORD had closed her womb.

original.text: וּלְחַנָּ֕ה יִתֵּ֛ן מָנָ֥ה אַחַ֖ת אַפָּ֑יִם כִּ֤י אֶת חַנָּה֙ אָהֵ֔ב וַֽיהוָ֖ה סָגַ֥ר רַחְמָֽהּ

verses.restored: Her rival provoked her intensely, to make her thunder/tremble, because YHWH had closed around her womb.

familiar.text: And her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the LORD had shut up her womb.

modern.text: Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her and taunt her viciously.

original.text: וְכִֽעֲסַ֤תָּה צָֽרָתָהּ֙ גַּם כַּ֔עַס בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְּעִמָ֑הּ כִּֽי סָגַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד רַחְמָֽהּ

verses.restored: So it happened year by year: as often as she went up to house of YHWH, the other provoked her. Hannah wept and would not eat.

familiar.text: And as he did so year by year, when she went up to the house of the LORD, so she provoked her; therefore she wept, and did not eat.

modern.text: And this went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival taunted her until she wept and would not eat.

original.text: וְכֵ֨ן יַעֲשֶׂ֜ה שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֗ה מִדֵּ֤י עֲלֹתָהּ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה כֵּ֖ן תַּכְעִסֶ֑נָּה וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תֹאכַֽל

verses.restored: Elkanah her husband said to her, Hannah, why do you weep, and why do you not eat, and why is your heart hurt? Am I not better to you than ten sons?

familiar.text: Then said Elkanah her husband to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

modern.text: “Hannah, why are you crying?” her husband Elkanah asked. “Why won’t you eat? Why is your heart so grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?” Hannah Prays for a Son

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֜הּ אֶלְקָנָ֣ה אִישָׁ֗הּ חַנָּה֙ לָ֣מֶה תִבְכִּ֗י וְלָ֨מֶה֙ לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְלִ֔י וְלָ֖מֶה יֵרַ֣ע לְבָבֵ֑ךְ הֲל֤וֹא אָֽנֹכִי֙ ט֣וֹב לָ֔ךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָ֖ה בָּנִֽים

verses.restored: Hannah rose after eating in Shiloh and after drinking. Eli the priest was sitting upon seat by doorpost of temple of YHWH.

familiar.text: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the LORD.

modern.text: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

original.text: וַתָּ֣קָם חַנָּ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְלָ֥ה בְשִׁלֹ֖ה וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁתֹ֑ה וְעֵלִ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֗ן יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל הַכִּסֵּ֔א עַל מְזוּזַ֖ת הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: She was bitter of soul, and she prayed to YHWH and wept greatly.

familiar.text: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore.

modern.text: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.

original.text: וְהִ֖יא מָ֣רַת נָ֑פֶשׁ וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל עַל יְהוָ֖ה וּבָכֹ֥ה תִבְכֶּֽה

verses.restored: She vowed a vow and said, YHWH of armies, if seeing, you will see affliction of your servant and remember me and not forget your servant, and give to your servant male offspring, then I will give him to YHWH all days of his life, and a razor shall not go up upon his head.

familiar.text: And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.

modern.text: And she made a vow, pleading, “O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever come over his head.”

original.text: וַתִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר וַתֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אִם רָאֹ֥ה תִרְאֶ֣ה בָּעֳנִ֣י אֲמָתֶ֗ךָ וּזְכַרְתַּ֨נִי֙ וְלֹֽא תִשְׁכַּ֣ח אֶת אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֥ה לַאֲמָתְךָ֖ זֶ֣רַע אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּנְתַתִּ֤יו לַֽיהוָה֙ כָּל יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו וּמוֹרָ֖ה לֹא יַעֲלֶ֥ה עַל רֹאשֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: As she multiplied praying before YHWH, Eli was watching her mouth.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli marked her mouth.

modern.text: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.

original.text: וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י הִרְבְּתָ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְעֵלִ֖י שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֶת פִּֽיהָ

verses.restored: Hannah was speaking upon her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Eli considered her intoxicated.

familiar.text: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.

modern.text: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk

original.text: וְחַנָּ֗ה הִ֚יא מְדַבֶּ֣רֶת עַל לִבָּ֔הּ רַ֚ק שְׂפָתֶ֣יהָ נָּע֔וֹת וְקוֹלָ֖הּ לֹ֣א יִשָּׁמֵ֑עַ וַיַּחְשְׁבֶ֥הָ עֵלִ֖י לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה

verses.restored: Eli said to her, How long will you make yourself drunk? Remove your wine from upon you.

familiar.text: And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.

modern.text: and said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ עֵלִ֔י עַד מָתַ֖י תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִ֑ין הָסִ֥ירִי אֶת יֵינֵ֖ךְ מֵעָלָֽיִךְ

verses.restored: Hannah answered and said, No, my lord. A woman hard-pressed in spirit am I. Wine and strong drink I have not drunk, but I have poured out my soul before YHWH.

familiar.text: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.

modern.text: “No, my lord,” Hannah replied. “I am a woman oppressed in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.

original.text: וַתַּ֨עַן חַנָּ֤ה וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲדֹנִ֔י אִשָּׁ֤ה קְשַׁת ר֨וּחַ֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וְיַ֥יִן וְשֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי וָאֶשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ אֶת נַפְשִׁ֖י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Do not give your servant as a daughter of worthlessness, because from abundance of my complaint and my provocation I have spoken until now.

familiar.text: Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.

modern.text: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”

original.text: אַל תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ לִפְנֵ֖י בַּת בְּלִיָּ֑עַל כִּֽי מֵרֹ֥ב שִׂיחִ֛י וְכַעְסִ֖י דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי עַד הֵֽנָּה

verses.restored: Eli answered and said, Go in peace, and may God of Israel grant your petition that you asked from him.

familiar.text: Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

modern.text: “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.”

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַן עֵלִ֛י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְכִ֣י לְשָׁל֑וֹם וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל יִתֵּן֙ אֶת שֵׁ֣לָתֵ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתְּ מֵעִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: She said, May your servant find favor in your eyes. The woman went on her way, ate, and her face was no longer as before.

familiar.text: And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.

modern.text: “May your maidservant find favor with you,” said Hannah. Then she went on her way, and she began eating again, and her face was no longer downcast. The Birth of Samuel

original.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר תִּמְצָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ הָאִשָּׁ֤ה לְדַרְכָּהּ֙ וַתֹּאכַ֔ל וּפָנֶ֥יהָ לֹא הָיוּ לָ֖הּ עֽוֹד

verses.restored: They rose early in morning, bowed down before YHWH, returned, and came to their house at Ramah. Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and YHWH remembered her.

familiar.text: And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.

modern.text: The next morning Elkanah and Hannah got up early to bow in worship before the LORD, and then returned home to Ramah. And Elkanah had relations with his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֛בוּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל בֵּיתָ֖ם הָרָמָ֑תָה וַיֵּ֤דַע אֶלְקָנָה֙ אֶת חַנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיִּֽזְכְּרֶ֖הָ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: It happened at turning of days that Hannah conceived and bore a son. She called his name Samuel, for she said, From YHWH I asked him.

familiar.text: Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD.

modern.text: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.”

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ לִתְקֻפ֣וֹת הַיָּמִ֔ים וַתַּ֥הַר חַנָּ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א אֶת שְׁמוֹ֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה שְׁאִלְתִּֽיו

verses.restored: The man Elkanah and all his house went up to sacrifice to YHWH the sacrifice of days and his vow.

familiar.text: And the man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the LORD the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.

modern.text: Then Elkanah and all his house went up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,

original.text: וַיַּ֛עַל הָאִ֥ישׁ אֶלְקָנָ֖ה וְכָל בֵּית֑וֹ לִזְבֹּ֧חַ לַֽיהוָ֛ה אֶת זֶ֥בַח הַיָּמִ֖ים וְאֶת נִדְרֽוֹ

verses.restored: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, Until the boy is weaned; then I will bring him, and he will appear before face of YHWH and remain there perpetually.

familiar.text: But Hannah went not up; for she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned, and then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD, and there abide for ever.

modern.text: but Hannah did not go. “After the boy is weaned,” she said to her husband, “I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.”

original.text: וְחַנָּ֖ה לֹ֣א עָלָ֑תָה כִּֽי אָמְרָ֣ה לְאִישָׁ֗הּ עַ֣ד יִגָּמֵ֤ל הַנַּ֨עַר֙ וַהֲבִאֹתִ֗יו וְנִרְאָה֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיָ֥שַׁב שָׁ֖ם עַד עוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: Elkanah her husband said to her, Do what is good in your eyes. Remain until you have weaned him; only may YHWH establish his word. So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.

familiar.text: And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Do what seemeth thee good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only the LORD establish his word. So the woman abode, and gave her son suck until she weaned him.

modern.text: “Do what you think is best,” her husband Elkanah replied, “and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.” So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהּ֩ אֶלְקָנָ֨ה אִישָׁ֜הּ עֲשִׂ֧י הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינַ֗יִךְ שְׁבִי֙ עַד גָּמְלֵ֣ךְ אֹת֔וֹ אַ֛ךְ יָקֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶת דְּבָר֑וֹ וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ וַתֵּ֣ינֶק אֶת בְּנָ֔הּ עַד גָּמְלָ֖הּ אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: When she had weaned him, she brought him up with her, with three bulls, one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. She brought him to house of YHWH at Shiloh, and the boy was young.

familiar.text: And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of the LORD in Shiloh: and the child was young.

modern.text: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.

original.text: וַתַּעֲלֵ֨הוּ עִמָּ֜הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר גְּמָלַ֗תּוּ בְּפָרִ֤ים שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ וְאֵיפָ֨ה אַחַ֥ת קֶ֨מַח֙ וְנֵ֣בֶל יַ֔יִן וַתְּבִאֵ֥הוּ בֵית יְהוָ֖ה שִׁל֑וֹ וְהַנַּ֖עַר נָֽעַר

verses.restored: They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.

familiar.text: And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.

modern.text: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ אֶת הַפָּ֑ר וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת הַנַּ֖עַר אֶל עֵלִֽי

verses.restored: She said, Please, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood beside you here, praying to YHWH.

familiar.text: And she said, Oh my lord, as thy soul liveth, my lord, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the LORD.

modern.text: “Please, my lord,” said Hannah, “as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י חֵ֥י נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֑י אֲנִ֣י הָאִשָּׁ֗ה הַנִּצֶּ֤בֶת עִמְּכָה֙ בָּזֶ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: For this boy I prayed, and YHWH gave me my petition that I asked from him.

familiar.text: For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him:

modern.text: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him,

original.text: אֶל הַנַּ֥עַר הַזֶּ֖ה הִתְפַּלָּ֑לְתִּי וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ אֶת שְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתִּי מֵעִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: So I, in turn, have lent/dedicated him to YHWH. All days that he lives, he is one lent/dedicated to YHWH. And he bowed down there to YHWH.

familiar.text: Therefore also I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD. And he worshipped the LORD there.

modern.text: I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.” So they worshiped the LORD there.

original.text: וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֨הוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כָּל הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֔ה ה֥וּא שָׁא֖וּל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ שָׁ֖ם לַיהוָֽה

translation_notes: Elkanah's family is called Ephrathite/Ephraimite in a genealogically and geographically difficult phrase; later audit should compare the Ramathaim, Zuph, and Ephrathite traditions.

Hannah's childlessness is never a moral failure, punishment formula, deficiency of womanhood, or evidence of lesser faith. The narrator's statement that YHWH closed her womb belongs to ancient theological narration and must not be weaponized against infertile or childless people.

Peninnah's provocation is harmful, but the text also places both women inside a polygynous household structured by unequal reproductive status and male distribution. Do not turn Peninnah into a misogynistic stereotype or use her motherhood against Hannah.
Elkanah loves Hannah and offers a special portion, yet his question in verse 8 cannot define what should be enough for her or dismiss grief with marital affection.
Hannah's refusal of food arises from distress and harassment. It is not a devotional fasting prescription, eating-disorder model, or proof that suffering makes prayer more effective.
Eli misreads silent prayer as drunkenness. Spiritual authorities must listen before labeling distressed people, and later correction does not erase the initial harm.
'Pouring out my soul' validates embodied lament, anger, complaint, and tears as prayer.

Hannah's vow is made under severe distress within an ancient household and sanctuary system. It must not justify parents dedicating children without consent, religious institutions claiming children, coercive vows, or bargaining away another person's future.
The no-razor clause evokes Nazirite traditions but is textually distinct from a complete Numbers 6 vow; later audit should compare witnesses and reception.
Elkanah 'knows' Hannah in a standard sexual idiom. The verse does not disclose consent language, though modern interpretation must never assume marriage eliminates the need for consent.
YHWH 'remembering' Hannah describes narrative attention, not prior forgetfulness and not a guarantee that prayer produces conception.
Samuel's name explanation is popular wordplay with sha'al, 'ask,' though the name itself is usually related to 'name of God' or 'heard by God.'
Weaning age and the textual variants in sacrifice animals require audit. The child's young age intensifies the ethical caution around dedication and separation.
The verb in verse 28 can mean lend, grant, or dedicate. Samuel remains a person, not property transferred between adults.
Hannah's agency is central: she prays, answers Eli, determines timing of weaning, accompanies Samuel, identifies herself, and interprets the dedication.
safety_note: Do not shame infertility, childlessness, grief, polygyny survivors, or eating under distress. Do not portray Peninnah as proof that women are inherently rivals. Do not use Hannah's vow to justify child dedication without consent, religious ownership of children, coercive parenting, or promises that prayer guarantees pregnancy. Preserve Hannah's lament, agency, and timing.
